result: Multiple immunizations (cohort-3x) resulted in physiological consolidation of antibody repertoires across lymphoid organs, characterized by equilibration of organ-specific features (germline V-gene usage and clonal expansion profiles), highly connected and overlapping B-cell clones, and reduced overall clonal diversity compared to single immunization (cohort-1x).
evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C41, C91, and C92 collectively demonstrate repertoire consolidation through multiple independent analyses: germline V-gene clustering (C41), clonal overlap quantification (C4, C46-C47), network connectivity (C42-C43), and diversity measurements (C32). The data from Figures 1-3 provide converging evidence across multiple mice (n=3 per cohort) using complementary analytical approaches.

result: Antibody repertoire consolidation directly correlated with antigen specificity, as demonstrated by yeast display screening showing that 88-95% of binding clones were shared across at least two organs, with 15-27% of clones shared across all six organs being antigen-specific, and shared binding clones displaying higher clonal frequencies.
evaluation: Claims C58-C66 provide experimental validation of the correlation between clonal overlap and antigen specificity through yeast display screening (120 binding clones detected) and Spearman correlation analysis (Figure 5e-f). The positive correlation is supported by quantitative data showing increased antigen-binding frequency with increased organ sharing. However, the yeast display approach uses random VH-VL pairing, which is a methodological limitation partially addressed by single-cell sequencing validation (C69).

result: Phylogenetic analysis revealed distinct physiological axes of B-cell migration: cohort-1x mice showed biased transitions from spleen to bone marrow and left-side lymph node connectivity, while cohort-3x mice exhibited bidirectional transitions between spleen and bone marrow, indicating more widespread clonal dispersal following multiple immunizations.
evaluation: Claims C52-C57 and C84 are supported by switch proportion (SP) test analysis on phylogenetic trees constructed using IgPhyML. The statistical significance (p<0.05) of directional transitions in cohort-1x versus bidirectional transitions in cohort-3x provides evidence for migration patterns. The left-side bias (C54-C56) is consistent with the immunization site. The phylogenetic approach appropriately accounts for clonal relationships and somatic hypermutation.

result: Cohort-3x mice exhibited a strong humoral response (average endpoint titer >1×10^6) compared to cohort-1x mice (average endpoint titer ~3×10^4), resulting in up to 70-fold increase in clonal overlap across all six lymphoid organs.
evaluation: Claims C24-C25 are supported by ELISA data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a) showing clear titer differences between cohorts. Claim C79 is supported by Venn diagram analysis (C46-C47) showing 1-3 shared clones in cohort-1x versus 49-71 in cohort-3x. The experimental design with n=3 mice per cohort and consistent results across biological replicates supports these findings.

result: Lymph nodes displayed lower clonal diversity (55-1055 unique clones) than bone marrow (1252-1846) and spleen (2475-3166), with cohort-3x showing reduced overall diversity per mouse when pooling all organs, increased bone marrow clonal diversity, and decreased spleen diversity compared to cohort-1x.
evaluation: Claims C26-C32 are supported by quantitative diversity measurements shown in Figure 1b-c with statistical testing (unpaired t-test, Benjamini-Hochberg correction). The control experiment with IgM+ clones from untreated mice (C27) addresses the concern that lymph node size alone explains reduced diversity. Subsampling analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f-g) confirms findings are not artifacts of sequencing depth.

result: Cohort-1x mice showed highly polarized clonal expansion in lymph nodes (Shannon evenness α=1E of 0.06, with top 3 clones comprising 33-71% of repertoire) compared to spleen and bone marrow, while cohort-3x mice exhibited uniform expansion across all organs (Shannon evenness 0.10-0.12, with top 3 clones at 15-32%).
evaluation: Claims C33-C37 are supported by Hill-based evenness analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a-b) and clonal expansion profiles (Figure 1d). The use of Hill diversity metrics is appropriate for comparing clonal frequency distributions. The consistent patterns across three mice per cohort strengthen the findings. Statistical significance is demonstrated through unpaired t-tests.

result: Cohort-3x mice displayed increased clonal connectivity, substantially higher clonal diversity in network analysis (particularly in spleen and bone marrow), higher somatic hypermutation counts across all organs, and substantial sharing of the five most diverse clonotypes across all six organs.
evaluation: Claims C42-C45 are supported by network analysis (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-c) and somatic hypermutation quantification (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a-b). The network approach using Hamming distance of 1 between CDRH3 sequences is appropriate for identifying clonal variants. The convergence of multiple metrics (connectivity, diversity, SHM, sharing) provides strong support.

result: Cohort-1x mice shared only 1-3 clones across all six organs with majority being organ-exclusive, while cohort-3x mice shared 49-71 clones with substantial sharing particularly in lymph nodes, showing greater repertoire similarity by Jaccard and cosine metrics, with physiological segregation along left/right lymph node and spleen/bone marrow axes.
evaluation: Claims C46-C51 are supported by Venn diagram analysis (Figure 3a), network visualization (Figure 3b), and similarity measurements (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b, Figure 3—figure supplement 2). The use of both Jaccard (presence/absence) and cosine (frequency-weighted) similarity provides complementary perspectives. The physiological axes are consistently observed across multiple analytical approaches.

result: Spleen and bone marrow contained more unique V-genes (99-115) than lymph nodes (31-92), displayed highest correlation in germline V-gene usage across both cohorts, and in cohort-1x the same organs of different mice clustered together with spleen and bone marrow showing highest similarity.
evaluation: Claims C38-C40 are supported by germline V-gene quantification and hierarchical clustering analysis (Figure 1e, Figure 1—figure supplement 2d). The use of Pearson correlation coefficients for V-gene usage is appropriate. The clustering patterns are consistent with the overall repertoire consolidation findings and provide orthogonal evidence for organ-specific versus mouse-specific repertoire features.

result: Single-cell antibody sequencing recovered 443-3416 IgG+ B cells per organ, revealed 26 clones shared across at least three organs and 157 shared across at least two organs, with 33% (6/18) of tested shared clones confirmed as antigen-specific.
evaluation: Claims C67-C69 are supported by 10x Genomics single-cell sequencing data (Figure 5g-h, Supplementary file 4-5, Figure 5—figure supplement 3b). The single-cell approach validates natural VH-VL pairing, addressing a limitation of the yeast display screening. The 33% antigen-specificity rate for shared clones provides independent validation of the correlation between sharing and specificity, though the sample size (18 tested) is modest.

result: In cohort-1x mice, extensive clonal expansion in lymph nodes suggests antigen-induced selection of IgG-switched B cells (possibly early germinal center B cells and short-lived plasmablasts), with distinct left/right physiological axes reflecting B-cell migration and/or antigen transport, and early homing to spleen and bone marrow, characterizing a weak humoral response with organ-exclusive repertoires.
evaluation: Claims C71-C78 integrate experimental observations (clonal expansion, overlap patterns) with mechanistic interpretations supported by citations to prior work (C72, C74, C76, C77). The inferences about cell types and migration are reasonable given the 10-day timepoint and IgG+ selection, though direct phenotypic characterization of the expanded cells was not performed. The characterization of weak response as organ-exclusive is well-supported by the overlap data.

result: High clonal overlap in cohort-3x mice may result from subcutaneous antigen drainage to lymph nodes and systemic circulation, migration of antigen-presenting cells and memory B cells, extensive clonal diversification consistent with refueling germinal center reactions, and dynamic behavior of long-lived plasma cells that may recirculate between bone marrow and spleen.
evaluation: Claims C80-C83 and C86-C88 are mechanistic interpretations supported by citations to prior work but not directly tested in this study. While the proposed mechanisms are plausible and consistent with the observed data, they remain speculative without direct experimental validation (e.g., tracking labeled cells, blocking migration pathways, phenotyping expanded populations). The extensive clonal diversification and SHM data (C82-C83) support ongoing germinal center activity, but direct evidence of germinal center refueling is not provided.

result: Spleen and bone marrow exhibited the highest repertoire similarity by sharing the majority of detected binding clones, and shared binding clones displayed relatively high clonal frequencies, consistent with oligoclonal B-cell responses upon vaccination.
evaluation: Claims C89-C90 are supported by yeast display screening data showing 74-86% of binding clones present in spleen (Figure 5c) and frequency analysis (Figure 5d-e). The observation is consistent with cited literature on oligoclonal responses (C90). However, the interpretation is limited by the random VH-VL pairing in the yeast display approach, though partially validated by single-cell data.

result: A shared (public) binding clonotype was present in all six lymphoid organs of all three cohort-3x mice, suggesting physiological consolidation and sequence convergence.
evaluation: Claim C64 is supported by experimental data from yeast display screening (Figure 5—figure supplement 2b). The detection of a public clonotype across all organs in all three mice provides strong evidence for convergent antibody responses. However, the functional significance and whether this represents true sequence convergence versus expansion from a common precursor is not definitively established.

result: Multiple immunizations may reduce antibody repertoire diversity across lymphoid organs, and future vaccine strategies may benefit from balancing humoral response strength with clonal repertoire diversity to facilitate greater antigen coverage and resistance to viral escape mutations.
evaluation: Claims C94-C96 are speculative extrapolations from the study findings to vaccine strategy implications. While the observation of reduced diversity with multiple immunizations is supported by data (C92), the functional consequences for breadth of antigen coverage and resistance to escape mutations are not tested. The speculation is reasonable but requires experimental validation in relevant infection/vaccination models with variant antigens.

result: Background claims establishing immunological context: antibody repertoires form the foundation of humoral immunity, B-cell development and migration pathways, serum titers reflect long-lived plasma cells, limited prior studies have profiled repertoires across multiple organs, and multiple immunization schemes are clinically employed.
evaluation: Claims C1-C2, C8-C23, C70, C85, and C93 are background knowledge claims supported by citations to established literature. These provide appropriate context for the study but do not represent novel findings. The knowledge gap statements (C14, C21) appropriately motivate the research questions.

result: Mice were subcutaneously injected at the left lateral flank with RSV-F antigen in poly(I:C) adjuvant, with cohort-3x receiving three injections at 21-day intervals.
evaluation: Claim C22 describes the experimental design, which is clearly documented in the methods section and Figure 1a. The design is appropriate for comparing weak versus strong humoral responses, with adequate sample size (n=3 per cohort) and proper controls.
